label: Semantic information types
summary: Semantic information types are the structured building blocks that make up a well-designed context window or information unit. Examples include instructions, prerequisites, concept explanations, checks and balances, factual data, cautions, and recommendations. Together they form self-contained, semantically labelled pieces of information that are machine readable, reusable, and traceable.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses semantic information types as the conceptual backbone for what she calls context design. She teaches students to include these types in system prompts with clear headings, arguing that a well-structured prompt works the same way a well-structured recipe does: it gives the model everything it needs, organised by what kind of information it is. She connects this directly to existing practices like information architecture, instructional design, and topic-based writing, making the case that context engineering is not a new discipline but a reframing of design work that already exists.
open_questions: Is there a definitive taxonomy of semantic information types, or does the set of types vary depending on the use case or domain?
How do semantic information types need to adapt when designing for API-integrated or multi-step agentic flows rather than single prompts?
